input.description: Overall odds ratio that significant and nonsignificant findings reported in special education dissertations would also be reported in corresponding journal publications
input.source_version_note: Publisher online-first article/proof from private Drive archive; final bibliographic pagination retained separately

blind.sample_role: Treatment/intervention outcomes (analytic observations), drawn from 40 dissertation–publication pairs; not individual participants.
blind.exclusions: Final pool follows exclusion of 167 dissertations lacking a corresponding publication and three during coding (one publication mismatch, one single-case design, one not an intervention). Only intervention-effect hypothesis tests extracted; pretest-equivalence, regression-assumption and correlational tests excluded. Overall model explicitly covers all 707 treatment outcomes.
blind.location: p. 7, Research Question 1 and Table 2; pp. 4–5, screening and extraction
blind.quote: odds ratio for the 707 treatment outcomes was 1.48 (with a ... 95% confidence interval ranging from 1.10 to 2.00).

disposition.reason: The RQ1 paragraph explicitly assigns 707 treatment outcomes to the overall Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio. Table 2 distinguishes 40 dissertation–publication pairs from 707 outcome observations.
disposition.location: p. 7, Research Question 1 and Table 2; p. 8, Discussion
disposition.quote: odds ratio for the 707 treatment outcomes was 1.48 (with a ... 95% confidence interval ranging from 1.10 to 2.00).
disposition.calculation: None; N directly printed. Analytic observations: 707 treatment outcomes; contributing study pairs: 40.

worker_target_description: RQ1 overall Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio comparing journal publication of statistically significant versus nonsignificant dissertation intervention outcomes.
worker_notes: Only assigned unfinished fields examined. Original side, reported_success, and unassigned replication fields are placeholders and must not overwrite previously verified fields. Source title and DOI match the supplied replication reference; publisher proof pagination used. Rendered PDF pages 7–8 inspected for layout. Overall analytic N=707 is directly printed, with 40 dissertation–publication pairs as source clusters; no summation or df inference used. The printed OR is 1.48 with 95% CI 1.10–2.00. No numeric p value/bound for this same overall OR is supplied; qualitative significance in the Discussion is not converted to a p bound. Moderator p values in Table 3 refer to different tests.

coding_context.description: Overall odds ratio that significant and nonsignificant findings reported in special education dissertations would also be reported in corresponding journal publications
coding_context.reported_success_quote: As expected, we found that the odds of a statistically significant outcome in a dissertation appearing in the published version were significantly greater than the odds of a nonsignificant outcome appearing in the published version, replicating (to some extent) the results obtained by Pigott and colleagues. Notably, the odds ratio we obtained (1.48) was smaller than that obtained by Pigott et al. (2.41), indicating a smaller outcome-reporting bias.

prior_adjudication.location: Online-first p. 7, Table 2 Note and Research Question 1
prior_adjudication.quote: Note. Outcomes obtained from N = 40 dissertations and corresponding … journal articles.
prior_adjudication.reason: The overall Mantel–Haenszel odds ratio is computed across 707 treatment outcomes (observation-level count) nested within N = 40 matched dissertation–journal article pairs (study/cluster-level count); because both counting units are valid and the target specification does not fix which level n_r represents, the field is undeterminable.
